note: FNS 850.5 covers workfare and comparable workfare programs, which are optional state programs where SNAP recipients perform work in exchange for benefits. Massachusetts does not operate a traditional workfare program — the term 'workfare' does not appear anywhere in the OLG, and CMR has no workfare regulations. Massachusetts does implement 'self-directed workfare' (community service) as one pathway for ABAWDs to meet ABAWD work rules, covered under 'ABAWD Work Rules Participation > Community Service.' However, FNS 850.5 is fundamentally a QC review procedure section: it instructs reviewers how to evaluate workfare disqualifications, verify noncompliance, handle variances (agency-caused errors), and assess exemptions — all QC audit methodology with no caseworker equivalent. The substantive policy elements (disqualification for noncompliance without good cause, good cause determinations, exemptions) are already covered by the OLG's General Work Rules and ABAWD Work Rules sections through their own disqualification and good cause frameworks. The ABAWD disqualification process (3-strike system via BEACON), good cause criteria, and community service participation/verification are all documented in the OLG. Since Massachusetts has no standalone workfare program and this section is QC procedure, it is not applicable.
